title: Popigai impact
summary: Approximately 36 to 35 million years ago during the Late Eocene, an asteroid roughly five to eight kilometers wide slammed into graphite-rich bedrock in northern Siberia. The hypervelocity collision created a crater approximately one hundred kilometers in diameter, tying as the fourth-largest verified impact structure on Earth. Intense shock compression instantly converted subterranean graphite into enormous deposits of polycrystalline impact diamonds, producing trillions of carats of ultra-hard industrial stones.

uncertainty.note: Radioisotopic dating of impact melt rock (tagamite) dates the collision to approximately 35.7 ± 0.2 Ma in the Late Eocene, commonly reported as 35 to 36 million years ago (NASA; Ohfuji et al. 2015).
